articles.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen
articles.dek: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St…
articles.description: Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 Aberdeen Kevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man Saints Derek McInnes asked his Rangers side to be “brilliant” against St Johnstone and was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. After dropping two points at Dundee last Saturday , the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy. Saints started the second half brightly but goals from Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by referee Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on midfielder Nico Raskin, before substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining. Continue reading...

Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games.

Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...
